title: Gilbert–Varshamov and Related Conjectures
scopeNotes: Five open problems centered on the Gilbert–Varshamov (GV) bound: the GV tightness question itself, explicit constructions meeting it, the asymptotic value of the Delsarte LP that yields the MRRW upper bound, the Euclidean analogue (Minkowski–Hlawka vs. Kabatiansky–Levenshtein), and explicit binary codes at list-decoding capacity. Not transcribed from an existing problem list; compiled from the literature with Devin. Each mathematicalConditions field states the minimal quantitative step that would count as progress rather than full resolution.

problems.problem: Is the binary Gilbert–Varshamov bound asymptotically tight?
problems.wordDescription: The Gilbert–Varshamov (GV) bound is the rate achieved by random (linear) binary codes and has not been improved by an exponential factor since the 1950s; the best upper bound is the MRRW linear-programming bound of 1977. Whether the truth is GV, MRRW, or strictly between is the central open question of asymptotic coding theory. Over alphabets of size \(q\ge 49\) (even prime powers) algebraic-geometry codes beat GV, and further improvements exist for other large \(q\), but for \(q=2\) no exponential improvement in either direction is known.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Let \(A_2(n,d)\) be the maximum size of a binary code of length \(n\) and minimum distance \(d\), and \(R(\delta)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\tfrac1n\log_2 A_2(n,\delta n)\). Known: \(1-H(\delta)\le R(\delta)\le R_{\mathrm{MRRW}}(\delta)\) for \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\), where \(H\) is binary entropy; the lower bound is improved only by sub-exponential factors (\(A_2(n,d)\ge c\,2^n\log_2 V(n,d-1)/V(n,d-1)\)). Minimal progress: exhibit one \(\delta_0\in(0,1/2)\) and a constant \(c>0\) with either \(R(\delta_0)\ge 1-H(\delta_0)+c\) (binary codes beating GV exponentially) or \(R(\delta_0)\le R_{\mathrm{MRRW}}(\delta_0)-c\) (an asymptotic improvement of the MRRW upper bound). Sub-exponential improvements of either side do not count.

literature.title: The q-ary Gilbert–Varshamov bound can be improved for all but finitely many positive integers q
literature.description: Shows \(R_q(\delta)>R_{\mathrm{GV}}(\delta,q)\) for all \(\delta\in[\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) once \(q\) is large enough (explicitly \(q>e^{29}\) at \(\delta=1/2\)), via Lenstra's codes from geometry of numbers; leaves small \(q\), in particular \(q=2\), untouched.

literature.title: An Improvement of the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound over Nonprime Fields
literature.description: GV is beaten for every nonprime field of order \(\ell\ge 49\) except possibly \(\ell=125\), within transitive and self-orthogonal codes as well.

literature.title: Asymptotic Improvement of the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound on the Size of Binary Codes
literature.description: Jiang–Vardy: \(A_2(n,d)\ge c\,2^n\log_2 V(n,d-1)/V(n,d-1)\) for \(d/n\le 0.499\) via local sparsity of the Gilbert graph; a factor-\(n\) but not exponential improvement.

literature.title: Towers of Global Function Fields with Asymptotically Many Rational Places and an Improvement on the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound
literature.description: Niederreiter–Xing: class field towers improve GV for sufficiently large composite nonsquare \(q\).

literature.title: Modular curves, Shimura curves, and Goppa codes, better than Varshamov–Gilbert bound
literature.description: Tsfasman–Vlăduț–Zink: algebraic-geometry codes from modular curves give \(R\ge 1-\delta-1/(\sqrt q-1)\), beating GV for square \(q\ge 49\).

literature.title: New upper bounds on the rate of a code via the Delsarte–MacWilliams inequalities
literature.description: McEliece–Rodemich–Rumsey–Welch: the first and second linear-programming bounds, still the best asymptotic upper bounds on \(R(\delta)\).

literature.title: A Comparison of Signalling Alphabets
literature.description: Gilbert's greedy/covering argument \(A_2(n,d)\ge 2^n/V(n,d-1)\); Varshamov (Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 117, 1957) obtained the same bound for linear codes.

problems.problem: Explicit binary codes on the Gilbert–Varshamov bound
problems.wordDescription: Random linear codes meet GV, but no deterministic polynomial-time construction is known to do so at any distance. In the high-distance regime \(\delta=(1-\varepsilon)/2\), equivalent to \(\varepsilon\)-biased sets of support \(O(k/\varepsilon^2)\), Ta-Shma's expander-walk construction reaches rate \(\varepsilon^{2+o(1)}\); the remaining \(o(1)\) is the frontier. The same regime carries the question of whether the true optimum is \(\Theta(\varepsilon^2)\) (GV) or \(\Theta(\varepsilon^2\log(1/\varepsilon))\) smaller (the MRRW-type lower bound on \(\varepsilon\)-biased sets).
problems.mathematicalConditions: Explicit means a deterministic \(\mathrm{poly}(n)\)-time algorithm outputting a generator matrix. Current frontier for relative distance \((1-\varepsilon)/2\): rate \(\varepsilon^{2}\cdot 2^{-O((\log\frac1\varepsilon)^{2/3}(\log\log\frac1\varepsilon)^{1/3})}\) (Ta-Shma); rate \(\varepsilon^2\cdot 2^{-(\log\frac1\varepsilon)^{\alpha}}\), \(\alpha\approx 1/2\), is known only under randomized or hypergraph-conditional constructions (Blanc–Doron). Minimal progress: an explicit family with relative distance \((1-\varepsilon)/2\) and rate \(\varepsilon^2\cdot 2^{-o((\log\frac1\varepsilon)^{2/3}(\log\log\frac1\varepsilon)^{1/3})}\); the target is rate \(\Omega(\varepsilon^2)\), or \(\tilde\Omega(\varepsilon^2)\) as an intermediate milestone. For fixed \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\) the corresponding minimal step is an explicit family with rate strictly above the Blokh–Zyablov bound at some \(\delta\).

literature.title: Gilbert and Varshamov Meet Johnson: List-Decoding Explicit Nearly-Optimal Binary Codes
literature.description: Richelson–Roy: polynomial-time list decoding of Ta-Shma's codes up to the Johnson bound, so the explicit near-GV codes are also algorithmically useful.

literature.title: New Near-Linear Time Decodable Codes Closer to the GV Bound
literature.description: Blanc–Doron: distance \(1/2-\varepsilon\) and rate \(\varepsilon^2\cdot 2^{-\log^{\alpha}(1/\varepsilon)}\), \(\alpha\approx1/2\), via walks on sparse hypergraphs; explicit only given sufficiently good explicit 3-uniform hypergraphs.

literature.title: Near-linear time decoding of Ta-Shma's codes via splittable regularity
literature.description: Jeronimo–Srivastava–Tulsiani: near-linear-time unique decoding of Ta-Shma's codes.

literature.title: Explicit, almost optimal, epsilon-balanced codes
literature.description: Ta-Shma: explicit \(\varepsilon\)-biased sets of support \(k/\varepsilon^{2+\alpha}\), \(\alpha=O((\log\log\frac1\varepsilon/\log\frac1\varepsilon)^{1/3})\), via long walks on the \(s\)-wide replacement product; the current explicit frontier.

literature.title: Simple Constructions of Almost k-wise Independent Random Variables
literature.description: Alon–Goldreich–Håstad–Peralta: explicit \(\varepsilon\)-biased sets of size \(O(k^2/\varepsilon^2)\) and \(O(k/\varepsilon^3)\), and the \(\Omega(k/(\varepsilon^2\log(1/\varepsilon)))\) lower bound via MRRW.

problems.problem: Asymptotic optimum of Delsarte's linear program for binary codes
problems.wordDescription: All known asymptotic upper bounds on binary code rate come from Delsarte's LP, yet the LP's own asymptotic value \(R_{\mathrm{LP}}(\delta)\) is unknown: MRRW only exhibits a feasible dual solution. Samorodnitsky proved \(R_{\mathrm{LP}}\) is at least the average of GV and MRRW and conjectured equality, while numerical evidence (Barg–Jaffe) suggests \(R_{\mathrm{LP}}\) equals the first LP bound where that bound applies. Settling this determines whether GV can ever be proved via Delsarte's LP alone, and motivates the stronger hierarchies (Schrijver SDP; Coregliano–Jeronimo–Jones and Loyfer–Linial LPs) whose bounded levels have not yet yielded any asymptotic improvement over MRRW.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Let \(A_{\mathrm{LP}}(n,d)\) be the optimum of Delsarte's LP for binary codes and \(R_{\mathrm{LP}}(\delta)=\limsup_n\tfrac1n\log_2 A_{\mathrm{LP}}(n,\delta n)\). Known for \(\delta\in(0,1/2)\): \(\tfrac12\big(1-H(\delta)+R_{\mathrm{MRRW}}(\delta)\big)\le R_{\mathrm{LP}}(\delta)\le R_{\mathrm{MRRW}}(\delta)\). Minimal progress: one \(\delta_0\) and constant \(c>0\) with \(R_{\mathrm{LP}}(\delta_0)\le R_{\mathrm{MRRW}}(\delta_0)-c\) or \(R_{\mathrm{LP}}(\delta_0)\ge\tfrac12(1-H(\delta_0)+R_{\mathrm{MRRW}}(\delta_0))+c\). Hierarchy variant: for some fixed level \(k\) of the Schrijver or Coregliano–Jeronimo–Jones/Loyfer–Linial hierarchies, show its asymptotic value at some \(\delta_0\) is at most \(R_{\mathrm{MRRW}}(\delta_0)-c\).

literature.title: On the Difficulty to Beat the First Linear Programming Bound for Binary Codes
literature.description: Samorodnitsky: necessary conditions any Friedman–Tillich-style dual solution must satisfy to beat the first LP bound, explaining the barrier.

literature.title: One more proof of the first linear programming bound for binary codes and two conjectures
literature.description: New proof of the first LP bound plus two conjectures whose truth would improve it.

literature.title: New LP-Based Upper Bounds in the Rate-vs.-Distance Problem for Binary Linear Codes
literature.description: Loyfer–Linial: a family of LPs for linear codes with Delsarte's LP as weakest member, numerically much stronger; asymptotics of bounded levels open.

literature.title: A Complete Linear Programming Hierarchy for Linear Codes
literature.description: Coregliano–Jeronimo–Jones: LP hierarchy for linear codes that converges to the true rate at finite level, with Delsarte's LP at the base.

literature.title: Linear Programming Bounds for Codes via a Covering Argument
literature.description: Navon–Samorodnitsky: recovers the first LP bound by Fourier duality and a covering argument, identifying it with an isoperimetric constant of the Hamming cube.

literature.title: New Code Upper Bounds From the Terwilliger Algebra and Semidefinite Programming
literature.description: Schrijver: SDP strengthening of Delsarte's LP via triples of codewords; improves finite-\(n\) bounds, asymptotics unresolved.

literature.title: Generalized Alon–Boppana Theorems and Error-Correcting Codes
literature.description: Friedman–Tillich: first LP bound for linear codes via spectral (Alon–Boppana) arguments.

literature.title: On the Optimum of Delsarte's Linear Program
literature.description: Samorodnitsky: \(R_{\mathrm{LP}}\ge\) average of GV and MRRW, so Delsarte's LP cannot prove GV; conjectures equality with the average.

literature.title: Numerical results on the asymptotic rate of binary codes
literature.description: Barg–Jaffe: numerical evidence that MRRW is asymptotically all Delsarte's LP yields in the first-LP range.

problems.problem: Is the Minkowski–Hlawka sphere-packing bound exponentially tight?
problems.wordDescription: The Minkowski–Hlawka bound \(\delta_n\ge 2^{-n}\) is the Euclidean analogue of GV: a random-lattice/greedy argument that has only been improved by polynomial factors, while the best upper bound is the Kabatiansky–Levenshtein LP bound \(2^{-(0.599+o(1))n}\), the analogue of MRRW. Whether the packing density is \(2^{-(1+o(1))n}\) or exponentially larger is open, and opinions differ (Torquato–Stillinger conjecture exponentially denser disordered packings).
problems.mathematicalConditions: Let \(\delta_n\) be the maximum density of a packing of equal balls in \(\mathbb R^n\). Known: \(c\,n^2 2^{-n}\le\delta_n\le 2^{-(0.599+o(1))n}\) (Klartag, lattice; Kabatiansky–Levenshtein with constant-factor refinements by Cohn–Zhao, Sardari–Zargar, Zargar). Minimal progress: either \(\delta_n\ge 2^{-(1-c)n}\) for some constant \(c>0\) and all large \(n\) (any exponential improvement over Minkowski–Hlawka), or \(\delta_n\le 2^{-(0.599+c)n}\) for some \(c>0\) (any improvement of the Kabatiansky–Levenshtein exponent). Polynomial-factor improvements on either side do not count.

literature.title: Lattice packing of spheres in high dimensions using a stochastically evolving ellipsoid
literature.description: Klartag: lattice packings of density \(\ge c\,n^2 2^{-n}\), the current best lower bound (Invent. Math. 2026).

literature.title: Stiefel manifolds and upper bounds for spherical codes and packings
literature.description: Zargar: improves the Kabatiansky–Levenshtein density bound by a factor \((1+o(1))/e\); exponent unchanged.

literature.title: A new lower bound for sphere packing
literature.description: Campos–Jenssen–Michelen–Sahasrabudhe: non-lattice packings of density \((1-o(1))\,n\log n/2^{n+1}\), the first growing improvement over Rogers since 1947.

literature.title: New upper bounds for spherical codes and packings
literature.description: Sardari–Zargar: first explicit uniform constant-factor improvement of the Kabatiansky–Levenshtein bounds.

literature.title: Sphere packing bounds via spherical codes
literature.description: Cohn–Zhao: constant-factor improvement of the Kabatiansky–Levenshtein packing bound.

literature.title: A note on sphere packings in high dimension
literature.description: Venkatesh: density \(\ge 65963\,n\,2^{-n}\), and \(n\log\log n\,2^{-n}\) along a sparse sequence of dimensions.

literature.title: New conjectural lower bounds on the optimal density of sphere packings
literature.description: Torquato–Stillinger: conjecture that disordered packings of density about \(2^{-0.7786n}\) exist, i.e. that Minkowski–Hlawka is not exponentially tight.

literature.title: On Bounds for Packings on a Sphere and in Space
literature.description: Kabatiansky–Levenshtein: LP bound \(\delta_n\le 2^{-(0.599+o(1))n}\), still the best exponent.

problems.problem: Explicit binary codes achieving list-decoding capacity
problems.wordDescription: Random binary codes of rate \(1-H(p)-\varepsilon\) are list-decodable from a \(p\) fraction of errors with list size \(O(1/\varepsilon)\), the GV-type existence result for list decoding. Over large alphabets folded Reed–Solomon codes achieve capacity explicitly, but for binary codes the best explicit polynomial-time-decodable tradeoff is the Blokh–Zyablov bound from multilevel concatenation, far below \(1-H(p)\); near \(p=1/2\) explicit rate is \(\Omega(\varepsilon^3)\) versus the capacity \(\Theta(\varepsilon^2)\).
problems.mathematicalConditions: For \(p\in(0,1/2)\), list-decoding capacity is \(1-H(p)\): random codes of rate \(1-H(p)-\varepsilon\) are \((p,O(1/\varepsilon))\)-list-decodable, and rate above \(1-H(p)\) forces exponential lists. Explicit frontier (deterministic \(\mathrm{poly}(n)\) construction with \(\mathrm{poly}(n)\) list decoding): the Blokh–Zyablov bound \(R_{\mathrm{BZ}}(p)\); at \(p=1/2-\varepsilon\) this gives rate \(\Omega(\varepsilon^3)\). Minimal progress: an explicit binary family, polynomial-time list-decodable from a \(p_0\) fraction of errors with polynomial list size, whose rate exceeds \(R_{\mathrm{BZ}}(p_0)\) by a constant at some \(p_0\); equivalently in the high-noise regime, rate \(\Omega(\varepsilon^{3-c})\) for some \(c>0\) at radius \(1/2-\varepsilon\). Purely combinatorial (non-algorithmic) explicit list-decodability beyond \(R_{\mathrm{BZ}}\) is a weaker acceptable step.

literature.title: Randomness-Efficient Constructions of Capacity-Achieving List-Decodable Codes
literature.description: Algebraic Wozencraft-type ensembles reaching the Elias bound \(R\ge1-H(\rho)-O(1/L)\) with \(O(Ln)\) random bits; explicit capacity-achieving binary codes remain open.

literature.title: Gilbert and Varshamov Meet Johnson: List-Decoding Explicit Nearly-Optimal Binary Codes
literature.description: Richelson–Roy: Ta-Shma's rate-\(\varepsilon^{2+o(1)}\) codes list-decoded in polynomial time up to the Johnson bound, radius \((1-\rho)/2\) for \(\rho\ge\sqrt\varepsilon\).

literature.title: Improved list-decodability of random linear binary codes
literature.description: Li–Wootters: random linear binary codes of rate \(1-H(p)-\varepsilon\) are list-decodable with list size \(H(p)/\varepsilon+2\), matching random codes.

literature.title: On the List-Decodability of Random Linear Codes
literature.description: Guruswami–Håstad–Kopparty: random linear codes achieve capacity with list size \(O(1/\varepsilon)\).

literature.title: Better Binary List-Decodable Codes via Multilevel Concatenation
literature.description: Guruswami–Rudra: explicit binary codes list-decodable in polynomial time up to the Blokh–Zyablov bound; the current explicit frontier.

literature.title: Explicit Codes Achieving List Decoding Capacity: Error-Correction With Optimal Redundancy
literature.description: Guruswami–Rudra: folded Reed–Solomon codes achieve capacity \(1-R-\varepsilon\) over large alphabets; concatenation gives explicit binary codes up to the Zyablov bound.

literature.title: Combinatorial bounds for list decoding
literature.description: Guruswami–Håstad–Sudan–Zuckerman: existence of binary linear codes of rate \(1-H(p)-1/L\) list-decodable with list size \(L\).

literature.title: Error-correcting codes for list decoding
literature.description: Elias: random-coding argument establishing list-decoding capacity \(1-H(p)\) (also Zyablov–Pinsker 1981).
